text:
alex: Ran an end-to-end profile on chat-compose (standard tier) and p95 is creeping to 320ms vs our 250ms target. Initial suspect: batch formation + kernel mismatch when sequence lengths spike.

mira: Ugh. Saw the same in yesterday's run. KV hitrate dropped ~8% during the spike window, which seems to increase effective tokens in-flight.

jonah: Can you paste the flame output? I want to see where the time is going (kernel vs queue wait).

alex: Paste of the trimmed profiler: 
```
flame: queue_wait 0.12s | kernel_attn 0.08s | kv_lookup 0.04s | kernel_ff 0.06s | io 0.02s
note: during spikes queue_wait jumps to ~0.2s and kernel_attn increases slightly due to longer sequences
```

lina: Two quick hypotheses: 1) continuous batcher is over-slicing small requests into too many microbatches -> queue head spend; 2) kernel selection fallback (fp16->int8 path) is triggering under particular seqlen distributions causing more copies.

alex: Agreed. I instrumented the batch fabric: when seqlen variance > 0.6 we currently keep microbatch_target=32 which seems suboptimal. Proposed: dynamic microbatch_target = clamp(8, 32, 16 * median_seqratio). Also change queue policy to `elastic_slice` (prefer filling by token budget not request count).

mira: Nice. Also saw kv-warmup cold starts for some routes; we could bias cache prefetch for 'chat-compose' hot prefixes. That should recover ~4-6% p95.

jonah: What about kernel routing? We could add a cheap heuristic: if avg_seqlen > 512 and batch_size_tokens > 4096 force the higher-throughput kernel (even if quantized path slightly worse for quality). It's a controlled fallback for p95.

alex: Draft config snippet for canary: 
```yaml
batch_fabric:
  mode: elastic_slice
  microbatch_target_fn: ">=16*median_seqratio, max 32, min 8"
  token_budget_by_tier:
    enterprise: 12000
    standard: 6000
    free: 3000
kernel_routing:
  seqlen_threshold: 512
  token_threshold: 4096
  prefer_kernel: high_throughput_if_over_threshold: true
kv:
  prefix_prefetch:
    chat-compose: true
    ttl_s: 1800
```

lina: Looks good. Need a guardrail: add a soft rollback if p95 improves but accuracy eval on our canary subset drops >0.5% for top-1 match.

infra-bot: canary-deploy queued for team=eng-runtime, env=staging, id=canary/3123456790. Expected finish: 15m.

mira: Running local replay now with the config on a 10% sampled trace. Early numbers: p95 down to 260ms, kv hitrate +5%, but tail errors on rare long sequences rose slightly.

jonah: Keep the canary but add a route-tier override: reduce token_budget for free tier to avoid noisy tails. Also add `safety_cutoff_ms: 600` for long-running requests to trigger graceful fallback (reduce max tokens).

alex: I'll kick the canary, add rollback monitors: p95, kv-hitrate, top1-accuracy. If any regresses beyond thresholds we auto-roll back.

lina: After canary, let's schedule a perf regression postmortem if anything regresses. Also log a perf flag in the model registry for kernel hinting.

alex: Thanks team. I'll post results in this thread when the canary finishes. :thumbsup:
